Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html

## Vue[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#vue)

This guide shows how to point a Vue app at Pinstripe's ESLint and Prettier presets.

### Install[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#install)

Add Pinstripe as a dev dependency:

```
npm install --save-dev @waynestate/pinstripe eslint prettier
```

### Configure ESLint[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#configure-eslint)

Create `eslint.config.js` and spread the preset. For TypeScript:

```js
import pinstripe from '@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/typescript'

export default [...pinstripe]
```

For plain JavaScript, import `@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/javascript` instead.

### Configure Prettier[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#configure-prettier)

Point Prettier at the preset in `package.json`:

```json
{
    "prettier": "@waynestate/pinstripe/prettier"
}
```

### Add scripts[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#add-scripts)

Add scripts that run on every OS:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "lint": "eslint .",
        "format": "prettier --write ."
    }
}
```

`npm run lint` fails on style and accessibility. `npm run format` fixes the layout. The preset is the off-the-rack suit: it fits every app, and you only add your own cufflinks.

Note

If an app adopts Oxlint for speed, ESLint stays in the toolchain for `.vue` files, because Pinstripe's Vue and accessibility rules (eslint-plugin-vue and eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility) run only in ESLint.

### Related[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#related)

- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [The strict cut](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html)
- [Best practices](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/

## Overview[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#overview)

This page summarizes what Pinstripe is, shows the install and run commands, and points you to the guide for your stack.

### What Pinstripe is[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#what-pinstripe-is)

**Sharp code. Every line.**

The coding standard for the Wayne State app stack: shared presets for Pint, PHPStan (with Larastan for Laravel), Rector, and ESLint with Prettier. Your app points at them and adds only its own exceptions. Pinstripe is to code what a good suit is to a job interview: nobody notices it, everybody notices when it's missing.

It needs PHP ^8.3, runs PHPStan at level 8, and is MIT licensed. Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Note

**Not to be confused with:** Pinstripe is the code style settings you run locally; Preflight runs them, and PROCTOR, in CI. Pinstripe's Rector set modernizes code within the app's current PHP version, while Booster upgrades the app to a newer PHP version.

### Install and run[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install-and-run)

In your app, add Pinstripe as a dev dependency, then run the checks:

```bash
composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true
composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.1
composer lint
composer fix
composer analyse
```

`composer lint` fails on style. `composer fix` fixes it. `composer analyse` runs PHPStan at level 8, with deprecation checks too.

### Pick your path[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html): point PHPStan at the raw config and Pint at the `per` preset.
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html): the Laravel preset, with Larastan registered for you.
- [Vue](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html): the ESLint and Prettier presets for JavaScript, TypeScript and Vue.
- [Rector](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html): modernize code for the PHP version your app already supports.
- [Tested with](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html): the tool versions Pinstripe is tested with, and the floors each tool needs.

### Status[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

The repository is at version 0.1.4. The npm package, `@waynestate/pinstripe`, follows each tag at the same version, published by hand. The canonical repository is on git.wayne.edu; GitHub is a read-only push mirror of it, and Packagist and npm read from it. The agent-ready site ships a plain-text twin for machines: [llms.txt](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt).

### Related[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#related)

- [Upgrading](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html)
- [Contributing](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html)
- [Changelog](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html

## Best practices[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#best-practices)

This page lists every rule Pinstripe holds itself to and the tests that prove each one.

How Pinstripe keeps its own promises: every preset is enforced by a test that runs the real tool against a fixture, so a preset that stops working fails `composer ci` here instead of failing a developer's app. A preset without a test is a suit without a mirror: you cannot tell when it has gone wrinkled.

A preset is **Enforced** when a test asserts both directions: a clean fixture passes, and a deliberately broken one is caught. The PHP presets run under `composer ci` (PHPUnit); the JavaScript presets run under `npm test`. Both run in CI on GitLab and GitHub, so a preset that stops working fails the pipeline before it reaches an app.

### `pint/per.json` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#pint-per-json)

Pint, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testPintPerPresetAcceptsTheCleanFixture`
- `PresetsTest::testPintPerPresetRejectsTheMessyFixture`

### Pint GitLab output[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#pint-gitlab-output)

Pint, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testPintGitlabFormatReportsTheMessyFixtureAsCodeQualityJson`
- `PresetsTest::testPintGitlabFormatIsAnEmptyArrayForTheCleanFixture`

### `pint/laravel.json` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#pint-laravel-json)

Pint, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testPintLaravelPresetAcceptsTheLaravelAppFixture`

### `pint/per-strict.json` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#pint-per-strict-json)

Pint, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testPintPerStrictPresetAcceptsTheStrictTypesCleanFixture`
- `PresetsTest::testPintPerStrictPresetRejectsTheStrictTypesMissingFixture`

### `pint/laravel-strict.json` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#pint-laravel-strict-json)

Pint, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testPintLaravelStrictPresetRejectsTheStrictTypesMissingFixture`

### `phpstan/raw.neon` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#phpstan-raw-neon)

PHPStan, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigAcceptsTheCleanFixture`
- `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigReportsTheNullBug`

### `phpstan/laravel.neon` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#phpstan-laravel-neon)

PHPStan + Larastan, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetLoadsLarastanThroughTheExtensionInstaller`
- `PresetsTest::testPhpStanLaravelConfigAcceptsTheLaravelAppFixture`
- `PresetsTest::testPhpStanLaravelConfigReportsTheUndefinedEloquentProperty`

### Larastan env() rule[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#larastan-env-rule)

PHPStan + Larastan, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetReportsAnEnvCallOutsideConfig`
- `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetAcceptsAConfigCallOutsideConfig`

### PHPStan ignore comments[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#phpstan-ignore-comments)

PHPStan, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigReportsAnIgnoreWithoutAComment`
- `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigReportsAnIgnoreThatMatchesNothing`
- `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigAcceptsAnIgnoreWithAComment`

### `rector/base.php` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#rector-base-php)

Rector, Enforced.

- `PresetsTest::testRectorPresetAcceptsTheCleanFixture`
- `PresetsTest::testRectorPresetReportsChangesOnTheOldFixture`

### `eslint/javascript.js` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#eslint-javascript-js)

ESLint, Enforced.

- `tests/js/presets.test.mjs` (`npm test`)

### `eslint/typescript.js` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#eslint-typescript-js)

ESLint, Enforced.

- `tests/js/presets.test.mjs` (`npm test`)

### `prettier/index.json` [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#prettier-index-json)

Prettier, Enforced.

- `tests/js/prettier.test.mjs` (`npm test`)

### README "Tool floors"[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#readme-tool-floors)

composer.lock + package-lock.json, Enforced.

- `ToolFloorsTest::testToolFloorsMatchTheLockFiles`

## Proof[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page says how Pinstripe was proven on real Wayne State applications: what ran, what held, what the run caught in Pinstripe itself, and what it does not prove yet. Next, see [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html) for the path the run followed and [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html) for the baseline rules.

A suit is proven at the fitting, not on the hanger. So on 2026-11-05 the presets were fitted to every PHP application in the stack's shared proof corpus, the same set PROCTOR, Squire and Preflight are measured on.

### Last run[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` (all five) | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: 67 tests, 382 assertions, 1 skipped, exit 0 | 744 s |
| `composer validate --strict` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: composer.json is valid | under 1 s |
| `php bin/agent-ready.php --check` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: 22 agent-ready files current | 1 s |
| `composer audit` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: no security vulnerability advisories found | 1 s |
| `php bin/docs-site.php --check` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: 17 docs pages current | 3 s |

To refresh this table, regenerate the site with `composer docs` and `composer site:agent-ready`, rerun `composer ci`, and rewrite the rows with the new counts and the commit you ran on. The 82-application proof run described below did not run here: its corpus of internal application repositories is not reachable from this machine, and the npm side (ESLint and Prettier for Vue) runs in the npm-test CI job, not in `composer ci`.

### What ran[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-ran)

Pinstripe 0.1.3, the presets as they are on `main`, with PHP 8.4. The 82 applications are 64 raw PHP apps (33 with a `composer.json`, 31 without one), 17 Laravel apps from 5.8 to 13, and 1 Slim 2 app. Laravel apps got the `laravel` presets; every other app got `per` and `raw`.

Each app was a throwaway copy of its default branch, checked out with Linux line endings, with `.env` files, `auth.json` and `config.files/` removed. Packagist was reachable; every Wayne State host was mapped to `127.0.0.1`, so nothing private could be fetched. Then, for each app:

1. Pint in test mode with the shape's preset, on the whole app, with a 15 minute limit;
2. for an app with a `composer.json`, the install the README gives: `composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.1`, plus `larastan/larastan` for Laravel, and once more with `-W` when Composer itself said a locked package was in the way;
3. PHPStan with the preset: inside the app when the install worked, and otherwise, for a raw app, from a separate Pinstripe install pointed at the app's files;
4. where the install worked and PHPStan found errors: a baseline generated with `--generate-baseline`, PHPStan run again with it, and `pinstripe-baseline count` on it.

An app **passes** when Pint and PHPStan are both clean. It is **flagged** when either reports findings, or when the install could not finish for a reason the app owns. A **tool error** is a crash, a timeout, a report that is not valid, or a Pinstripe command that does not do what it says.

### Results[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#results)

| Units | Pass | Flagged | Tool error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 82 applications | 0 | 81 | 1 |

No application was clean on day one, which is what a coding standard adopted late looks like. The tool error is a Pint timeout, described below.

| Step | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| Pint | Ran on all 82 apps and finished on 81, every one with findings: a median of 14 files to restyle, at most 180. The median app took 2 seconds. |
| Install | 12 of the 51 apps with a `composer.json` installed Pinstripe, one of them only with `-W`. The other 39 stopped on the app's own dependencies: 36 install a package from a private Git repository that the run could not reach, 2 need a PHP extension the run did not have, and for 1 Composer refused the update because the app's locked framework has security advisories. |
| PHPStan | Ran on 66 apps (12 inside the app, 54 raw apps from the separate install) and finished on all 66 with errors at level 8: a median of 86, at most 6,721. No crash, no memory limit hit. The median app took 11 seconds. The 16 Laravel apps that could not install were not analysed, because Larastan needs the app's own framework. |
| Baselines | Generated on all 12 apps that installed. With the baseline, PHPStan was green on 10. On the other 2 PHPStan said some errors could not be put into a baseline (classes that extend a class it could not find). `pinstripe-baseline count` read every baseline, and its count plus the errors PHPStan could not baseline equals PHPStan's total on every app. |

### What it caught in Pinstripe[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-caught-in-pinstripe)

A run that only finds praise was not looking hard enough. This one found these, and every finding is about Pinstripe, not the apps:

- **Fixed: `pinstripe-baseline count` printed an app's deprecations.** Installed in an app, the command loads the app's autoloader, and one app's old HTTP library printed PHP 8.4 deprecations ahead of the count. A script reading the number got a page of warnings. The command now mutes deprecations while it loads the autoloader, and a test covers it.
- **Documented: `-W`.** The install line failed on an app that already locked an older PHPStan, and Composer's own advice, `-W`, fixed it. The README and the guides now say so.
- **Documented: what a baseline cannot hold.** [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html) now says what to do when PHPStan cannot baseline an error, and how to keep Pint off a library the app bundles.
- **Open: Pint on bundled libraries.** One app bundles a PDF library whose generated font maps are single arrays hundreds of kilobytes long. Pint spent over 100 seconds on one such file and did not finish the app in 15 minutes. That is Pint's fixer, not Pinstripe's preset, and the guide's advice is to point Pint at your own folders.
- **Open: Laravel apps that cannot install.** Larastan analyses a Laravel app through its framework, so an app whose dependencies cannot install gets no PHPStan result at all, while a raw app still gets one from a separate install.

### What this does not prove[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-this-does-not-prove)

- No app adopted Pinstripe for real: nothing was committed, and the restyling Pint proposed was not applied or reviewed.
- No private package could be fetched, so 36 apps never got past the install, and 16 Laravel apps were not analysed.
- The npm side (ESLint and Prettier for Vue) did not run here.
- The per-app record names the applications and stays in the stack's internal notes.

### Run it on your app[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#run-it-on-your-app)

The same steps on your own app, from its root:

```sh
composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true
composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.1
vendor/bin/pint --test --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per.json
vendor/bin/phpstan analyse
```

For a Laravel app, add `larastan/larastan` to the `require` line and use `pint/laravel.json`. Then follow [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html) to baseline what is there and keep the new code clean.

### Related[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#related)

- [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html)
- [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html)
- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html

## Tested with and tool floors[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html#tested-with-and-tool-floors)

This page records the tool versions Pinstripe is tested with and the PHP or Node floor each locked tool declares.

### Tested with[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html#tested-with)

- Pint 1.32.1
- PHPStan 2.3.3
- PHPStan extension-installer 1.4.3
- PHPStan strict-rules 2.1.0
- Larastan 3.13.2
- Rector 2.8.2
- ESLint 10.13.0
- Prettier 3.9.10
- eslint-plugin-vue 10.12.0
- eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility 2.6.3
- typescript-eslint 8.72.1
- Node 22, 24 and 26 (the JS presets run in CI on all three; the floor stays 22.13)

### Tool floors[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html#tool-floors)

Can your app run Pinstripe's tools? Each row shows the floor the locked package itself declares, read verbatim from `composer.lock` and `package-lock.json` today and checked against them by `tests/ToolFloorsTest.php`, so a dependency bump forces a README update in the same change.

PHP tools:

| Tool | Locked version | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `laravel/pint` | v1.32.1 | `^8.3.0` |
| `phpstan/phpstan` | 2.3.3 | `^7.4\|^8.0` |
| `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules` | 2.1.0 | `^7.4 \|\| ^8.0` |
| `phpstan/phpstan-deprecation-rules` | 2.0.5 | `^7.4 \|\| ^8.0` |
| `larastan/larastan` | v3.13.2 | `^8.2` |
| `rector/rector` | 2.8.2 | `^7.4\|^8.0` |

Node tools:

| Tool | Locked version | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eslint` | 10.13.0 | `^20.19.0 \|\| ^22.13.0 \|\| >=24` |
| `eslint-plugin-vue` | 10.12.0 | `^18.18.0 \|\| ^20.9.0 \|\| >=21.1.0` |
| `typescript-eslint` | 8.72.1 | `^18.18.0 \|\| ^20.9.0 \|\| >=21.1.0` |
| `prettier` | 3.9.10 | `>=14` |

- Pinstripe itself needs PHP 8.3 or newer and Node 22.13 or newer, so the Pint floor is the binding PHP floor.
- Pint only reads and rewrites files, so an app still on an older PHP can run Pint with a PHP 8.3 or newer binary (for example a container) while the app itself keeps its runtime.
- ESLint 10 is what sets the Node floor: Node 20 before 20.19 is out.

Measure twice, cut once: these floors are cut from the lock files, and the test keeps the hem honest.

### Related[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html#related)

- [Best practices](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)
- [ADR-0001: PHPStan level 8 and baselines](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/adr/0001-phpstan-level-and-baseline-policy.html)
- [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html)
- [Changelog](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html

## Upgrading[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

This page walks through each released version of Pinstripe, what changed for consumers, and how to verify the upgrade.

### What a stricter preset means to you[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#what-a-stricter-preset-means-to-you)

A stricter preset breaks consumers' builds. Pinstripe ships such a change in a minor version, not a major one, so you opt in by updating the package. When a version below marks a change as breaking, it is a stricter preset taking effect in your app the moment you update to it; hold the current version until you are ready.

### 0.1.4 (2026-11-06)[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-4-2026-11-06)

**Breaking (three tailoring changes, each a stricter fit):**

- `pinstripe-baseline` counts or checks a baseline only when the app's `composer.json` carries `"extra": { "pinstripe": { "legacy": true } }`. A baseline is for apps adopting Pinstripe late; new apps never set the flag.
- The ESLint presets (`@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/javascript` and `/typescript`) fail lint on every Vue and accessibility finding: rules the plugins' recommended configs report as warnings are now errors, so the editor, a local `npm run lint` and CI agree. Apps that need the old behavior for a while spread `@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/javascript-warn` or `/typescript-warn` instead.
- The Prettier preset formats Blade views with `prettier-plugin-blade` (pinned to 3.3.3). The first run rewrites every `*.blade.php` file (4-space indent, a space after directive names such as `@vite (`, void tags self-closed), so reformat in a commit of its own.

**Steps:** Your constraint is `^0.1`, which already allows 0.1.4, so update the locked version of `waynestate/pinstripe` to 0.1.4 (and `@waynestate/pinstripe` to 0.1.4 once it is on npm; check with `npm view @waynestate/pinstripe version`). If you use `pinstripe-baseline`, add the `legacy` flag first. Copy the two `.npmrc` lines from the README's "Supply chain" section into your app. To see ESLint findings in merge requests, run `eslint --format gitlab`.

**How to verify:** `composer analyse` and `npm run lint` pass (or list the findings you now own), `pinstripe-baseline check` still counts your baseline, and `npx prettier --check "resources/views/**/*.blade.php"` passes after the one-time reformat.

### 0.1.3 (2026-11-03)[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-3-2026-11-03)

No breaking change. The one change that touches your app is that the install instructions now include `composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true`, so a non-interactive install works. The remaining items (the docs site, the ADR, the Node 22, 24 and 26 test matrix, the `laravel-vue` fixture, and the CI and deploy pins) are internal to Pinstripe.

### 0.1.2[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-2)

**Breaking (Laravel apps):** `phpstan/laravel.neon` now pins Larastan's `noEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig` rule on, so an `env()` call outside `config/` fails analysis. This is a stricter preset shipped in a minor version, so you opt in by updating rather than being forced into a breaking major.

**Steps:** Your constraint is `^0.1`, which already allows 0.1.2, so update the locked version of `waynestate/pinstripe` to 0.1.2.

**How to verify:** Run `composer analyse` in your app. Any `env()` call outside `config/` is now reported; read config with `config()` instead, because once the config is cached `env()` returns null.

### 0.1.1[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-1)

No breaking change: this release only removes reports the raw and Laravel cuts should never have made. It fixes the raw and Laravel PHPStan cuts inheriting `reportMaybesInMethodSignatures` and `reportStaticMethodSignatures` from `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules`, which made them report phpdoc method signature issues they should not; `base.neon` now pins both to false and `strict.neon` keeps them on. It also pins the other eight parameters `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules` forces on: four low-noise ones stay on in every cut, and `checkDynamicProperties`, `reportMaybesInPropertyPhpDocTypes`, `reportWrongPhpDocTypeInVarTag` and `reportNonIntStringArrayKey` are off in `base.neon` and on in `strict.neon`.

**Steps:** Your constraint is `^0.1`, which already allows 0.1.1, so update the locked version of `waynestate/pinstripe` to 0.1.1.

**How to verify:** Run `composer analyse` in your app. The raw and Laravel cuts no longer report the inherited phpdoc method signature issues.

### 0.1.0[#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-0)

First release, so there is nothing to break. It adds `bin/pinstripe-baseline`, which counts a PHPStan baseline's ignored errors (`count`) and fails when the baseline grows (`check --max=<n>` or `check --against=<git-ref>`), so baselines only shrink. It adds `phpstan/strict.neon`, an opt-in PHPStan preset for new apps that turns on `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules`, and adds `tests/fixtures/per`, a Pint fixture proving the `per` preset is the PER Coding Style.

**Steps:** Add Pinstripe as a dev dependency with `composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.1`, then wire the presets into your app.

**How to verify:** In your app, run `composer lint` and `composer analyse` once the presets are wired in.
